title: Nominate an address (challenge + proof-of-work)
purpose: Submit a listing nomination. Nothing is listed until review, or until 5 distinct nominators agree.
line_docs: interpreter line; run this file directly
Nominate one IPv4 address: get a challenge, solve the proof-of-work, POST /api/v1/nominations.
Usage: ./06-nominate.sh <ipv4> [reason]
Documentation, private, and reserved addresses are rejected with HTTP 400.
Leave company_url empty; that field is a honeypot.
A live POST of 192.0.2.10 on 19 Nov 2026 returned 400 with that reserved-address message.
exit on error, unset variable, or a failed pipe
set IPRX_BASE to use a different API host
address to nominate; default is TEST-NET (will be rejected)
at least 8 characters
set IPRX_NAME to your display name
set IPRX_EMAIL to your address; used to count distinct nominators
fetch a fresh one-time challenge
Solve SHA-256(challenge + ":" + nonce) with at least `bits` leading zero bits (usually 18).
NONCE="$(CH_JSON="$CH_JSON" python3 -c '
import hashlib, json, os
ch = json.loads(os.environ["CH_JSON"])
challenge, bits = ch["challenge"], int(ch["bits"])
while True:
digest = hashlib.sha256(f"{challenge}:{n}".encode()).digest()
zeros = 0
for b in digest:
zeros = zeros + 8 if b == 0 else zeros + (8 - b.bit_length())
if b != 0:
break
if zeros >= bits:
print(n)
break
extract the opaque string
BODY="$(IP="$IP" REASON="$REASON" NAME="$NAME" EMAIL="$EMAIL" CHALLENGE="$CHALLENGE" NONCE="$NONCE" python3 -c '
import json, os
print(json.dumps({
"ip": os.environ["IP"],
"reason": os.environ["REASON"],
"evidence": "TEST",
"name": os.environ["NAME"],
"email": os.environ["EMAIL"],
"org": "IPRX docs examples",
"challenge": os.environ["CHALLENGE"],
"pow_nonce": os.environ["NONCE"],
"company_url": "",
NominationIn JSON; company_url must stay empty
curl -sS -X POST "${BASE}/api/v1/nominations" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
201 on success, 400 for TEST-NET
add a trailing newline

expected_response.detail: private, reserved, documentation, or operator-owned addresses cannot be nominated

notes: Live test: POST of 192.0.2.10 returned HTTP 400 with this detail. Use a public IPv4 you have evidence for. company_url must stay empty. Rate limit: 10 nominations per hour.

Usage: ./07-removal.sh <ipv4> [reason]
A successful request returns 201 with status pending_dkim and a one-time token.
The token is also written to a private local file (600); do not commit or share it.

while True:
digest = hashlib.sha256(f"{challenge}:{n}".encode()).digest()
zeros = 0
for b in digest:
zeros = zeros + 8 if b == 0 else zeros + (8 - b.bit_length())
if b != 0:
break

print(n)

nonce so SHA-256(challenge:nonce) has enough leading zero bits
extract the opaque string

"challenge": os.environ["CHALLENGE"],

RemovalIn JSON; company_url must stay empty
RESP="$(curl -sS -X POST "${BASE}/api/v1/removals" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
201 pending_dkim when healthy
print the JSON (includes a token — keep it private)
Save the token next to the event_id with mode 600, under $HOME, never in the repo.
python3 -c '
import json, os, pathlib, sys
resp = json.loads(sys.argv[1])
token = resp.get("token")
event_id = resp.get("event_id") or "unknown"
if not token:
raise SystemExit(0)
path = pathlib.Path.home() / ".iprx" / f"{event_id}.token"
path.parent.mkdir(mode=0o700, exist_ok=True)
path.write_text(token + "\n")

expected_response.message: Removal request recorded and stamped, but it will not move to admin review until you prove control of a domain tied to this IP. Upload a raw .eml …

notes: Live test: HTTP 201 pending_dkim. The token is saved to ~/.iprx/<event_id>.token (mode 600) and is redacted here. Next step is ./10-dkim-upload.sh. Removals are not applied automatically.

title: Upload a DKIM-signed .eml for a removal request
purpose: Prove control of a domain tied to the IP by uploading a raw RFC822 message. This script does not send email.
line_docs: interpreter line; run this file directly
Upload a DKIM-signed .eml to prove domain control for a removal request.
Usage: ./10-dkim-upload.sh <event_id> <message.eml>
The .eml must be a raw RFC822 message, DKIM-signed by the PTR host's registrable
domain or the RDAP/WHOIS org/abuse-contact domain, and must contain the one-time
token from POST /api/v1/removals in the subject or body.
This script only uploads a local file; it does not send any email.
A failed check is recorded and stamped; the request does not advance until a check passes.
After a pass, the request still waits for an operator decision.

set IPRX_BASE only if you are talking to a different host
from the removal response
local file; we never send mail for you
the file must exist and not be empty

-H "Accept: application/json" \
multipart field name is eml
add a trailing newline

expected_response._comment: A failed check is recorded and stamped; the request stays pending_dkim or becomes dkim_failed until a passing check.

notes: The .eml must contain the one-time token and be DKIM-signed by the PTR host's registrable domain or the RDAP/WHOIS org/abuse-contact domain. See samples/removal-proof.eml (template only, not signed).

title: Bulk-nominate IPs from a fail2ban (or similar) block file
purpose: Parse a local block file and submit each public IPv4 as a nomination, with a challenge and proof-of-work per IP.
line_docs: interpreter line; run this file directly
Nominate every public IPv4 address in a local block file via the IPRX API.
Usage:
./submit-blockfile.sh --dry-run ../samples/fail2ban.log
./submit-blockfile.sh --limit 3 --email you@example.org --name "Your Name" bans.txt
This bash entry point runs the documented Python submitter so every supported
format is parsed the same way: fail2ban status/banned/log, plain IP and CIDR
lists, CSV with ip,reason, ipset save, iptables-save, nftables sets, CrowdSec
`cscli decisions list -o json`, hosts.deny, Apache/nginx deny rules, and
Spamhaus DROP-style `ip ; comment` lines.
Flags (passed through unchanged):
--dry-run                 parse and print, do not call the API
--limit N                 nominate at most N eligible addresses
--reason TEXT             default reason when the file has none
--email / --name / --org  your identity (required for a live submit)
--delay SECONDS           pause between live posts (default 1)
--output FILE             append per-IP results JSONL (event_id, receipt_url)
--format auto|...         force a parser; auto is the default
--max-cidr-size 256       refuse to expand a prefix larger than this
--submit-documentation    TEST ONLY: also POST RFC 5737 TEST-NET addresses
(the API rejects them with HTTP 400)
--base URL                default https://iprx.org
Private, reserved, loopback, and documentation addresses are skipped.
Duplicates are dropped. The live API allows 10 nominations per hour; the
script honours HTTP 429. One submitter email counts as one nominator toward
the 5-distinct-nominator listing threshold, no matter how many IPs are in the file.
A batch nomination endpoint would avoid one proof-of-work per IP; it is not in this release.
exit on error, unset variable, or a failed pipe
directory of this script, so we can find ../python
the reference submitter (every line is commented)
the tree is incomplete
tell the user where we looked
stop
fi
replace this process; all flags are documented above
notes: This bash entry point runs the Python reference submitter. One submitter email counts as one nominator toward the 5-distinct-nominator threshold. The API allows 10 nominations per hour. A batch endpoint would help; it is not in this release. TEST-NET sample files are all skipped (or, with --submit-documentation, POSTed and rejected with HTTP 400).

title: Request a one-click API token email
purpose: Ask IPRX to email a one-click link that issues a verified API token. Opening the link shows the token once. The same email can hold several labeled tokens.
line_docs: interpreter line; run this file directly
Request a one-click email that issues an IPRX API token.
Usage: IPRX_EMAIL=you@example.com ./12-token-request.sh [label]
The email comes from veraetimestamp@gmail.com. Opening the link shows the token once.
First-time requestors create a billing-disabled Verae account and must accept the license.
501(c)(3) nonprofits and schools must upload documentation via POST /api/v1/accounts instead.
This script does not print or store the token; it only asks the API to send the email.
exit on error, unset variable, or a failed pipe
set IPRX_BASE to use a different API host
required: the address that should receive the link
optional label, for example laptop or honeypot-1
org size for first-time account setup
fetch a fresh one-time challenge
solve the SHA-256 proof-of-work
POST /api/v1/tokens/request
202 if the email was accepted for sending

expected_response.message: If the address is valid, a one-click confirmation email is on its way. The link expires in 30 minutes.

notes: The response never includes the token or the magic link. Set IPRX_ORG_SIZE if you are not a private individual. Tokens are sent as Authorization: Bearer iprx_… and skip the proof-of-work; verified-token nominations have no rate limit. Never commit a live token.
